Subject: Consortium integration — MSA/DPA/SOW redline review

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time on the call yesterday — excited about Vectorium joining the consortium for our integration pilot.

Attached are the baseline agreements we typically use for ISV consortium integrations: Redwood_MSA_v3.docx, Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf, and a short SOW (Redwood_SOW_Integrator.docx) that scopes the technical onboarding and support milestones.

Key asks from our side:
- Can you send redlines on the MSA/DPA/SOW by COB Monday so we can route to legal and procurement?
- High-level items we expect to discuss: data residency carveouts (EU), liability cap alignment, and audit scope for security/compliance.

If it helps your team, we have SOC 2 Type II evidence available and can add a narrow audit window rather than open-ended audit rights. Also happy to discuss a limited liability multiple tied to annual fees.

Attaching the docs — let me know if procurement needs additional paperwork (PO templates, W9, etc.). Looking to keep timelines tight: aim for signed MSA before end of November if possible.

Best,

Soojin Lee | Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.com | soojin@redwood.com

From: Sarah Turner <sarah@vectorium.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom@vectorium.com>, Vectorium Labs Procurement <procurement@vectorium.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Consortium integration — MSA/DPA/SOW redline review

Soojin,

Thanks for sending these over. I've attached Vectorium_Redlines_20261101.docx with our initial comments — high level summary below:

1) Data residency & transfer: We need a firm commitment that Vectorium customer data originating in the EU will remain in EU regions and will not be processed in non-EU jurisdictions without prior written consent. Standard SCCs + technical measures acceptable, but prefer explicit contract language clarifying processing locations and subprocessors.

2) Liability & indemnity: Our legal asks to reduce open-ended indemnities related to model outputs. Specifically, we propose: (a) carve out third-party IP claims that arise from Vectorium-supplied customer data; (b) mutual limitation of liability with a cap tied to 12 months of fees and standard exclusions (fraud, willful misconduct).

3) Audit & evidence: Vectorium agrees to SOC 2 Type II as the baseline. We request audit rights be scoped to one audit per 12 months, with a 30-day notice and mutually agreeable auditor. We cannot accept broad continuous access to systems or on-site inspections.

4) Security incident notifications: 72-hour notification window for security incidents impacting customer data; we propose a triage timeline and point-of-contact.

5) SOW: we redlined the milestone schedule and acceptance criteria to reflect a 10-week integration timeline and SLA for first-response support.

We're generally aligned but will need Redwood's legal to confirm acceptable language around residency and the liability cap. Please route to Karthik and Vanessa as needed and let us know if you prefer to handle via DocuSign or a marked-up Word doc.

Regards,

Sarah Turner
Legal Counsel, Vectorium Labs
Attachments: Vectorium_Redlines_20261101.docx (docx)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Sarah Turner <sarah@vectorium.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Consortium integration — MSA/DPA/SOW redline review

Sarah / team — appreciate the thorough redlines. Internal quick take and proposed compromise below.

Summary of Redwood position (recommended):
- Residency: Accept explicit EU residency commitment for Vectorium-originated customer PII and model training inputs. We will list permitted regions (EU/US) and agree to run processing in EU only for EU tenants unless Vectorium provides written consent to cross-border processing. We will also provide subprocessors list and 30-day notice for changes.

- Liability / Indemnity: Propose mutual indemnities with the following limits: liability cap equal to the greater of 3x annual fees or $1M, carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct. For IP claims tied to customer-supplied data, we will limit Redwood liability and require notice and an opportunity to defend. This is a middle ground between your 12-month cap and our standard multiple.

- Audit: Agree to SOC 2 Type II plus one third-party audit per 12 months with 30-day notice. We will not permit intrusive on-site inspections as a baseline.

- Incident notifications: We can commit to a 48-hour notification for incidents impacting customer data, with a prioritized remediation plan.

- SOW: Accept updated timeline but request a slightly expanded acceptance window (7 business days) to allow for integration verification on our side.

Next steps:
1) If Vectorium agrees to the compromise above, we will produce a tracked-counter (Redwood_CounterRedlines_20261102.docx) and circulate for signature.
2) If you need to escalate the liability cap figure, please indicate operational or procurement constraints — we can route to finance for concession analysis.

Soojin / Karthik — please confirm and I will finalize the counter. We aim to keep the November signature target but will need procurement alignment on the cap.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz | Head of Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
